# 1. What the Research Found

**MONITORING. Re-check window: retrieve the IEA Electricity Mid-Year Update 2025 full PDF and the IEA Electricity 2025 February flagship report to complete headline-figure population; re-check the EU ENTSO-E recommendation adoption status in Q4 2026.**

This finding synthesises the IEA Electricity Mid-Year Update 2025 alongside four corroborating authoritative sources captured for this pass: the IEA Renewables 2025 report (renewable capacity pipeline and grid-integration challenges), the U.S. EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook (U.S. electricity demand and price corroboration), and the ENTSO-E Expert Panel Final Report on the 28 April 2025 Iberian Blackout (grid-security event analysis).

*Note on primary source access:* the primary source URL (https://iea.org/reports/electricity-mid-year-update-2025) returned no extractable content in this capture pool. FACT claims below are drawn only from source blocks with extractable content; headline figures attributed to the mid-year update itself are recorded as gaps in Section 5 where no verbatim span is available.

FACT: "Policy changes in the United States, macroeconomic pressures and supply chain challenges have raised costs and undermined project bankability in several European markets and Japan, resulting in undersubscribed auctions and project cancellations. As a result, we have revised the global offshore wind capacity forecast 27% downwards from last year." *Source: Renewables 2025, Renewable Electricity, IEA. https://www.iea.org/reports/renewables-2025/renewable-electricity

FACT: "Distributed solar PV applications (residential, commercial, industrial and off-grid projects) account for 42% of the overall PV expansion." *Source: Renewables 2025, Renewable Electricity, IEA. https://www.iea.org/reports/renewables-2025/renewable-electricity

FACT: "Growth in utility-scale and distributed solar PV more than doubles, representing nearly 80% of worldwide renewable electricity capacity expansion." *Source: Renewables 2025, Renewable Electricity, IEA. https://www.iea.org/reports/renewables-2025/renewable-electricity

FACT: "The US forecast is revised down by almost 50% across all technologies except geothermal." *Source: Renewables 2025, Renewable Electricity, IEA. https://www.iea.org/reports/renewables-2025/renewable-electricity

*Analytical inference:* the pattern across these four sourced revisions (a global 27% offshore-wind downward revision, a US-specific ~50% downward revision across nearly all technologies, and a global capacity-expansion pipeline still dominated 80% by solar) reads as a US-policy-driven regional slowdown layered onto an otherwise-intact global solar buildout, not a uniform global deceleration.

# 2. Why This Finding Matters Operationally and Commercially

FACT: "Renewable electricity additions for 2025-2030 total 4 600 GW – equal to the combined installed power capacity of China, the European Union and Japan" *Source: Renewables 2025, Renewable Electricity, IEA. https://www.iea.org/reports/renewables-2025/renewable-electricity

*Operational implication:* for workspaces evaluating SAF or electric ground-handling commitments, which depend on the long-run electricity price outlook, the US-specific downward revision to renewables forecasts (Section 1) represents a material shift in the supply-side assumptions that underpin "cheap renewable electricity" scenarios used in SAF cost modelling and electric fleet business cases.

FACT: "Electricity demand growth is led by growth in the commercial sector , which is expected to outpace residential demand in 2027 for the first time on record." *Source: Short-Term Energy Outlook, U.S. Energy Information Administration. https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/

FACT: "Residential electricity prices are expected to increase by 5% in 2026 and to continue to rise in 2027, although at a slower pace." *Source: Short-Term Energy Outlook, U.S. Energy Information Administration. https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/

*Operational implication:* for workspaces operating energy-intensive logistics infrastructure in the United States (warehousing with active climate control, cold-chain facilities, ground-support equipment charging for air-primary operations), the confirmed 5% residential electricity price increase in 2026, with commercial-sector demand growth outpacing residential demand for the first time on record, signals upward pressure on operational electricity costs across the Americas trade lane. The East Coast concentration of the largest price increases is directly relevant to air freight hub operations and distribution centres in that corridor.

*Operational implication:* the Iberian blackout of 28 April 2025 is a documented, expert-investigated grid-failure event. For workspaces with logistics nodes, bonded warehouses, or time-critical air freight operations routing through Madrid or Lisbon hubs, the event establishes a concrete precedent for grid-failure-driven operational disruption relevant to EU-corridor continuity planning.

# 3. What the Finding Changes for Strategy, Claims, or Decisions

**1. Renewable procurement assumption review.**

*Analytical inference:* the combination of a US-specific ~50% downward revision and offshore wind's global 27% downward revision (Section 1) narrows the pipeline of new renewable capacity available for corporate power-purchase-agreement or renewable-energy-certificate procurement. Workspaces that have made client-facing commitments on the basis of "abundant cheap renewable electricity" timelines should verify that their procurement assumptions remain valid under the revised IEA and EIA forecasts.

**2. US facility electrification cost planning.**

FACT: "Residential electricity prices are expected to increase by 5% in 2026 and to continue to rise in 2027, although at a slower pace. Prices are rising across the United States, but the largest increases will likely occur in regions along the East Coast." *Source: Short-Term Energy Outlook, U.S. Energy Information Administration. https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/

*Operational implication:* workspaces planning US facility expansions, particularly warehouse electrification, EV charging for road fleets, or SAF production partnerships, should factor the forecast 5% price increase in 2026 into capital expenditure and operating cost models.

**3. EU grid-resilience-dependent operations.**

*Analytical inference:* the ENTSO-E panel's investigation of the Iberian blackout (Section 2) is a forward signal that EU grid codes and network regulations are likely to be revised in response to the event. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether and when specific ENTSO-E recommendations will be incorporated into binding EU network codes, and what compliance obligations this creates for grid-connected infrastructure operators in Spain, Portugal, or wider continental Europe, requires legal and regulatory review as the European Commission and national regulators respond.

# 4. Client Conversation Talking Points and Public Position

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- The Iberian blackout of 28 April 2025 is a documented, expert-investigated event; a formal panel report on it has since been published. Workspaces can reference this publicly available report when discussing supply-chain resilience with clients operating EU corridor routes.
- Global renewable capacity additions of nearly 4 600 GW are projected for 2025-2030, doubling the pace of the prior five years, per the IEA's own sourced figure. This is directly citable.
- The EIA forecasts a 5% US residential electricity price increase in 2026, with commercial demand growth leading the market for the first time on record; this is a citable government forecast appropriate for client cost conversations.

**Pitfalls to avoid:**

*Analytical inference:* avoid claiming that the Iberian blackout "proves" European renewable integration is failing; the sourced investigation identifies a combination of operational, coordination, and regulatory factors rather than a simple renewable-penetration failure thesis. Overstating the finding risks undermining credibility with technically literate clients.

*Analytical inference:* avoid presenting the US renewables downward revision as a global story; the captured sources are clear that this is a US-specific policy effect (Section 1), not a universal slowdown narrative.

# 5. What the Finding Does Not Resolve

GAP: [methodology_limits] Key headline figures attributed to the IEA Electricity Mid-Year Update 2025 itself, including global electricity demand growth actuals for H1 2025, wholesale price revisions, and half-year emissions figures specific to the mid-year update, are not present in the captured source blocks; the primary source URL returned no extractable content in this capture pool.

GAP: [methodology_limits] Detailed EU grid-adequacy figures for summer 2025 are not present in the captured source blocks.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] Whether and when specific ENTSO-E recommendations will be incorporated into binding EU network codes, and what compliance obligations this creates for grid-connected infrastructure operators in Spain, Portugal, or wider continental Europe, is not established from the captured source blocks; this is a matter for legal and regulatory review as the European Commission and national regulators respond.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] SAF and clean-fuel cost implications: the electricity-price and renewable-deployment findings above are relevant inputs to SAF cost modelling and electric-fleet business cases, but the captured source blocks do not resolve those downstream, cargo-vertical-specific calculations.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] Converging or contradicting research from the IEA's prior flagship Electricity report, the baseline the mid-year update is understood to revise, is not present in the captured source blocks.

# 1. What the Research Found

**MONITORING. Re-check window: the blocked IEA Global Hydrogen Review sub-pages (Investment and Innovation, Trade and Infrastructure, Breakthrough Agenda) at 30 days from this pass; re-check accessibility periodically.**

**Headline finding:** the global clean hydrogen industry has reached a capital-commitment inflection point, over $110 billion committed across 510 projects, but is structurally constrained by an offtake gap: only approximately 60% of committed project capacity has binding demand contracts, and the pathway to 9-14 Mtpa by 2030 depends on policy implementation, not technology availability.

**Methodology and scope:** the Hydrogen Council Global Hydrogen Compass 2025 combines project-level industry data with Hydrogen Council member input and CEO-level perspectives, co-authored with McKinsey and Co analytical support. Its scope is global clean hydrogen supply, demand, investment, and policy. It does not cover fossil hydrogen or unabated grey hydrogen economics in the same analytical frame.

FACT: "Committed (FID+ including FID, under construction, and operational projects) investment in clean hydrogen has now passed $110 billion across 510 projects, up $35 billion from last year and growing on average over 50% year-over-year since 2020." *Source: Global Hydrogen Compass 2025, Hydrogen Council. https://hydrogencouncil.com/en/global-hydrogen-compass/

FACT: "Of the 6 mtpa of committed clean hydrogen capacity today, 1 mtpa is already operational." *Source: Global Hydrogen Compass 2025, Hydrogen Council. https://hydrogencouncil.com/en/global-hydrogen-compass/

FACT: "After accounting for delays and expected attrition, the current project pipeline could support up to 9-14 mtpa of clean hydrogen capacity by 2030, depending on how much supply secures offtake." *Source: Global Hydrogen Compass 2025, Hydrogen Council. https://hydrogencouncil.com/en/global-hydrogen-compass/

FACT: "Approximately 3.6 mtpa of binding offtake is in place today globally, representing about 60% of committed project capacity." *Source: Global Hydrogen Compass 2025, Hydrogen Council. https://hydrogencouncil.com/en/global-hydrogen-compass/

FACT: "Looking ahead to 2030, about 8 mtpa of 2030 clean H2 demand could materialize in the EU, US, Japan, and Korea, but requires that existing policies are implemented and enforced." *Source: Global Hydrogen Compass 2025, Hydrogen Council. https://hydrogencouncil.com/en/global-hydrogen-compass/

FACT: "Advancement of projects with the strongest business cases is expected to be coupled with cancellations of less viable projects as the pipeline continues to mature." *Source: Global Hydrogen Compass 2025, Hydrogen Council. https://hydrogencouncil.com/en/global-hydrogen-compass/

*Analytical inference:* the policy-conditional phrasing in the 2030 demand figure above (requiring existing policies to be implemented and enforced) is a genuine forecast qualifier, not a formality; the source itself treats policy continuity as a live variable rather than a settled assumption.

*Note:* the IEA Global Hydrogen Review 2025 sub-pages (Executive Summary, Investment and Innovation, Trade and Infrastructure) and the IEA Breakthrough Agenda Hydrogen chapter returned no extractable content in this capture pool; every FACT claim above is drawn from the Hydrogen Council capture, the one substantive source block available for this pass.

# 2. Why This Finding Matters Operationally and Commercially

For freight forwarding workspaces operating primarily in air, with road and ocean secondary, the hydrogen market's current structure (1 Mtpa operational, 6 Mtpa committed, 9-14 Mtpa conditional on offtake by 2030) directly determines when hydrogen-derived fuels (green ammonia, e-methanol, liquid hydrogen, and SAF produced via Power-to-Liquid pathways) become available at the volumes and price points that affect freight costs and client sustainability commitments.

*Operational implication:* the offtake gap between binding demand (3.6 Mtpa) and committed capacity (6 Mtpa) means a significant share of the projected clean hydrogen supply pipeline remains at risk of cancellation or delay. Workspaces whose client sustainability commitments depend on SAF scale-up, which relies partly on green hydrogen supply, should treat the 9-14 Mtpa 2030 range as a wide band, not a floor.

*Operational implication:* the policy-conditionality finding (8 Mtpa demand in the EU, US, Japan, Korea requiring existing policies to be implemented and enforced) connects directly to regulatory instruments a freight forwarding workspace already monitors: EU hydrogen mandates under FuelEU Maritime and ReFuelEU Aviation, US hydrogen production tax credit rules, and Japanese hydrogen strategy subsidies. If any of these policies weaken or are delayed, the demand side of the 2030 projection deteriorates.

*Analytical inference:* for workspaces whose air-freight clients operate under scope 3 reporting frameworks and have committed to SAF purchase agreements or book-and-claim arrangements, the hydrogen supply constraint is a second-order cost risk: SAF prices remain elevated until green hydrogen feedstock becomes available at scale, which this source's own analysis places at post-2030 for meaningful volumes.

# 3. What the Finding Changes for Strategy, Claims, or Decisions

**1. SAF procurement strategy and client commitments.**

*Analytical inference:* the offtake gap and project-attrition signal (Section 1) mean workspaces should not represent to clients that green hydrogen-derived SAF will be commercially available at scale in the near term; the sourced 9-14 Mtpa range by 2030 is conditional on policy, not a committed floor. Any client-facing commitment to SAF volumes that depends on Power-to-Liquid pathways should be qualified against this uncertainty.

**2. Supplier diversification across fuel pathways.**

*Analytical inference:* the source's explicit project-attrition signal (Section 1) should prompt workspaces advising clients on low-carbon logistics solutions to avoid concentrating commitments in a single fuel pathway; HEFA-SAF, synthetic SAF, and direct electrification for road segments represent differentiated exposure.

**3. Client sustainability reporting assistance.**

*Operational implication:* for workspaces providing emissions data and sustainability-reporting support to clients, the distinction between committed investment ($110 billion across 510 projects) and operational capacity (1 Mtpa) is a material disclosure point; clients claiming scope 3 improvements from green-hydrogen-derived fuels should be directed to the operational-only figure, not the committed-pipeline figure.

**4. Ocean lane bunkering risk monitoring.**

*Analytical inference:* the connection between hydrogen supply trajectory and ammonia or methanol bunkering availability on major ocean lanes is quantified enough to factor into carrier selection and tender language; carriers that have signed ammonia or methanol bunkering offtake agreements are better hedged than those whose net-zero vessel orders remain uncommitted on fuel type.

# 4. Client Conversation Talking Points and Public Position

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- "The clean hydrogen industry has crossed $110 billion in committed investment across 510 projects, with 1 Mtpa already operational; the infrastructure is being built, not just announced." Sourced to the Hydrogen Council Global Hydrogen Compass 2025.
- "The credible 2030 supply range is 9-14 Mtpa, conditional on both policy continuity and securing additional offtake contracts, not a guaranteed floor."
- "The critical gap right now is demand, not supply technology; a substantial share of committed capacity still lacks binding offtake."

**Questions to pose to clients:**

- Which SAF pathway are current book-and-claim agreements sourced from, HEFA, alcohol-to-jet, or synthetic/Power-to-Liquid? The answer determines exposure to hydrogen supply delays.
- Has the carrier base disclosed whether low-carbon vessel orders carry committed fuel offtake, or are they still uncommitted on fuel type?
- Are scope 3 reporting commitments timeline-matched to when green hydrogen supply is realistically available, or implicitly dependent on a pre-2030 Power-to-Liquid SAF scale-up?

**Pitfalls to avoid:**

*Analytical inference:* do not conflate committed investment ($110 billion) with operational capacity (1 Mtpa); the gap is the strategic point, and conflating them overstates readiness. Do not represent the 9-14 Mtpa 2030 range as a projection independent of policy; the source explicitly conditions it on securing offtake and on existing policies being implemented and enforced.

*Analytical inference:* the Hydrogen Council is an industry advocacy body, not a regulator; its findings carry weight as industry data but should be qualified as industry analysis in client-facing materials, not presented as IEA or governmental authority. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific client's fuel-purchase structure triggers any direct obligation under ReFuelEU Aviation or FuelEU Maritime requires counsel review.

# 5. What the Finding Does Not Resolve

GAP: [does_not_resolve] The specific IEA-attributed quantitative findings referenced in this pass's source inputs (global hydrogen demand, low-emissions share, FID pipeline figures, investment figures, pipeline infrastructure lengths, Germany repurposing status) are not present in the captured source blocks; the relevant IEA Global Hydrogen Review sub-pages returned no extractable content.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] How clean hydrogen supply constraints translate to specific SAF price trajectories by year or route is not present in the captured source blocks; this depends on carrier-specific and fuel-pathway-specific modelling not available from the source content accessed.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] Whether the uncommitted-offtake gap will be closed by policy-driven demand instruments or by market-driven offtake agreements is not present in the captured source blocks; the Hydrogen Council source flags this as an open, policy-dependent question.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] Emerging Market and Developing Economy financing barriers for hydrogen projects, referenced in the Breakthrough Agenda Hydrogen chapter, are not present in the captured source blocks; that chapter returned no extractable content in this capture pool.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] Certification and guarantees-of-origin standards for traded hydrogen and ammonia are not present in the captured source blocks; this is an unresolved question for workspaces whose clients make scope 3 claims on imported clean hydrogen derivatives.

GAP: [methodology_limits] The Hydrogen Council is an industry advocacy body whose membership includes hydrogen producers and offtakers with a commercial interest in the market's trajectory; the source itself is co-authored with McKinsey and Co analytical support, not an independent academic or government body.

GAP: [methodology_limits] The Hydrogen Council source does not cover fossil hydrogen or unabated grey hydrogen economics in the same analytical frame as clean hydrogen.

**Monitoring calendar (this research_finding's own timeline section, per its format's section list):**
- September 2025: the Global Hydrogen Compass 2025 was published, per the sourced date on this capture.
- 2030: the source's own conditional supply range (9-14 Mtpa, Section 1) and the policy-conditional demand figure (8 Mtpa in the EU, US, Japan, Korea, Section 1) both fall due; the next scheduled checkpoint for this forecast.

# 1. What the Research Found

**MONITORING. Re-check window: retrieve the IEA Global Supply Chains of EV Batteries PDF and the IEA EV Battery Supply Chain Sustainability follow-up to complete the quantitative grounding of this brief.**

**Headline finding: extreme geographic concentration creates systemic freight and supply-chain exposure.**

FACT: "Upstream: Mines extract raw materials; for batteries, these raw materials typically contain lithium, cobalt, manganese, nickel, and graphite. Midstream: Processors and refiners purify the raw materials, then use them to create cathode and anode active battery materials; commodities traders buy and sell raw materials to firms that produce battery cells. Downstream: Battery manufacturers assemble the battery cells into modules and then pack and sell them to automakers, who place the finished batteries in EVs. Some automakers like Ford and Stellantis have formed partnerships with battery manufacturers to produce their own batteries for the vehicles they sell. End of Life: When batteries no longer serve their original purpose, they can be reused or recycled." *Source: RMI, "The EV Battery Supply Chain Explained," May 5, 2023. https://rmi.org/the-ev-battery-supply-chain-explained/

FACT: "The EV battery supply chain is dispersed around the world — battery minerals travel an average of 50,000 miles from extraction to battery cell production." *Source: RMI, "The EV Battery Supply Chain Explained," May 5, 2023. https://rmi.org/the-ev-battery-supply-chain-explained/

FACT: "China currently dominates the supply chain. As broader geopolitical issues affect economic and trade relationships, the stability of the global supply chain is increasingly at risk when extracting, refining, processing, and assembling an outsized share of EV battery components occurs in any single country." *Source: RMI, "The EV Battery Supply Chain Explained," May 5, 2023. https://rmi.org/the-ev-battery-supply-chain-explained/

FACT: "this number will need to increase to 44 million by 2030 if we are to reach net-zero emissions." *Source: RMI, "The EV Battery Supply Chain Explained," May 5, 2023. https://rmi.org/the-ev-battery-supply-chain-explained/

entries.body:
# 1. What the Research Found

**MONITORING. Re-check window: retrieve the primary IRENA publication page and full report PDF (listed as corroborating sources, not yet accessible in this capture pool) to complete direct-source grounding of this brief.**

FACT: "91pc of newly commissioned utility-scale capacity delivering electricity cheaper than even the lowest-cost new fossil fuel capacity", per the International Renewable Energy Agency's report, Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2024. *Source: Argus Media, "Most new renewable energy cheaper than fossils: Irena," 23 July 2025. https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2713100-most-new-renewable-energy-cheaper-than-fossils-irena

FACT: the global weighted average LCOE for utility-scale solar photovoltaic power in 2024 was "USD 0.043" per kWh; "cheaper by 41pc than the lowest-cost fossil fuel-fired alternatives". *Source: Argus Media. https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2713100-most-new-renewable-energy-cheaper-than-fossils-irena

FACT: the global LCOE for onshore wind in 2024 was "USD 0.034" per kWh, "53pc cheaper than fossil fuel-based electricity". *Source: Argus Media. https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2713100-most-new-renewable-energy-cheaper-than-fossils-irena

FACT: "Solar and wind comprised 46.4pc of installed power generation capacity globally in 2024, displacing coal and gas in major markets like China, the EU and the US" *Source: Argus Media. https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2713100-most-new-renewable-energy-cheaper-than-fossils-irena

*Analytical inference:* the pattern across these sourced LCOE figures (solar and wind both now cheaper than fossil-fired alternatives, and both already comprising nearly half of installed global generation capacity) confirms the cost crossover cited in trade reporting is not a projection but a 2024 measured reality, per this source.

## Battery storage cost trajectory

FACT: "The total cost of utility-scale battery energy systems (BESS) has dropped by 93pc over 2010-24, according to the report" *Source: Argus Media. https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2713100-most-new-renewable-energy-cheaper-than-fossils-irena

FACT: "China currently dominates battery supply, producing over 75pc of global batteries at costs that are lower by 20-30pc compared with European and North American markets, according to the IEA" *Source: Argus Media. https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2713100-most-new-renewable-energy-cheaper-than-fossils-irena

FACT: "China and the US led global BESS growth in 2024, thanks to national policy incentives and grid integration mandates" *Source: Argus Media. https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2713100-most-new-renewable-energy-cheaper-than-fossils-irena

FACT: "But emerging geopolitical risks,especially trade tariffs on renewable components and materials, as well as Chinese manufacturing sector dynamics could lead to higher costs in the short term, Irena said." *Source: Argus Media. https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2713100-most-new-renewable-energy-cheaper-than-fossils-irena

## Technology-by-technology LCOE and regional asymmetry

FACT: geothermal LCOE fell from USD 0.072/kWh in 2023 (a 16% decrease); geothermal average capacity factor was 88% in 2024, up 7% from 2023, with values ranging from 77% to 88% since 2010. Hydropower LCOE was USD 0.057/kWh, concentrating solar power was USD 0.092/kWh, bioenergy was USD 0.087/kWh, and offshore wind was USD 0.079/kWh in 2024. *Source: ThinkGeoEnergy, "IRENA report highlights 16% decrease in geothermal power LCOE in 2024," 5 August 2025. https://www.thinkgeoenergy.com/irena-report-highlights-16-decrease-in-geothermal-power-lcoe-in-2024/

*Analytical inference:* weighted averages mask the wide project-level range visible in this source's own figures; geothermal alone ranged from USD 0.033/kWh at one location to USD 0.090/kWh at another in 2024. Workspaces procuring energy at depot, warehouse, or terminal level should obtain site-specific tariff data rather than relying on global weighted averages for investment decisions.

FACT: "582 GW of new capacity addition" in 2024, of which solar PV contributed 77.8% of the total; China accounted for 61.2% of global solar PV additions and 69.4% of new wind installations. *Source: ThinkGeoEnergy. https://www.thinkgeoenergy.com/irena-report-highlights-16-decrease-in-geothermal-power-lcoe-in-2024/

FACT: "Asia will likely retain a cost advantage but higher costs could persist in Europe and North America because of structural factors like delays in permits and higher balance-of-system costs." *Source: Argus Media. https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2713100-most-new-renewable-energy-cheaper-than-fossils-irena

FACT: "falling costs are not universal—developing countries, especially in Africa, face rising technology and finance costs due to weak policy support and high financing risks" and the report "warns of cost asymmetries across regions, which threaten global equity and decarbonization goals." *Source: Policy Commons / IRENA, "Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2024," 22 July 2025. https://policycommons.net/artifacts/22093445/irena_tec_rpgc_in_2024_2025/22993566/

FACT: "In 2023, renewables saved around USD 627 billion in fossil fuel costs, underlining their economic advantage" *Source: Policy Commons / IRENA. https://policycommons.net/artifacts/22093445/irena_tec_rpgc_in_2024_2025/22993566/

# 2. Why This Finding Matters Operationally and Commercially

*Operational implication:* for workspaces operating road-transport fleets serving high-value cargo verticals (fine art, luxury goods, live events equipment, high-value automotive), the sourced cost data confirms that grid-supplied renewable electricity is now structurally cheaper than fossil-fuel generation in most major markets. This shifts the economic argument for electric-fleet transitions from a sustainability premium toward cost parity or advantage, subject to local tariff structure.

*Analytical inference:* the battery-storage cost decline (Section 1) is the single most important data point for workspaces evaluating on-site solar-plus-storage at warehouse or depot facilities. However, the near-term tariff and geopolitical risk flagged above means procurement timing matters: sourcing in a tariff-escalation window increases capital cost and extends payback.

*Operational implication:* for workspaces with bonded warehouses, fine-art storage facilities, or live-events staging depots, renewable energy procurement is now economically defensible on cost grounds alone in markets where the sourced cost advantage has passed through to retail or commercial tariffs. The regional asymmetry finding (Section 1) means the workspace should not assume global LCOE averages apply to its specific facility locations; site-specific tariff benchmarking is the necessary next step before making procurement claims.

*Analytical inference:* the report does not directly address SAF or aviation fuels. However, the onshore-wind and solar LCOE figures above are a direct input to the economics of electrolytic hydrogen and Power-to-Liquid SAF pathways, which depend on low-cost renewable electricity as feedstock; this is an indirect connection, not a direct finding of this source.

*Operational implication:* for workspaces operating humanitarian cargo movements on African corridors, where this source explicitly documents rising technology and finance costs due to weak policy support and high financing risks, the renewable-energy cost advantage documented globally does not automatically apply; energy procurement costs for depot or cold-chain operations in affected regions should not be assumed to benefit from the LCOE declines visible in G20 markets.

# 3. What the Finding Changes for Strategy, Claims, or Decisions

**1. On-site solar and BESS investment appraisal is now standard procurement, not speculative.**

*Analytical inference:* the battery-storage cost reduction (Section 1) is a sourced, verifiable data point that moves the threshold analysis for depot solar-plus-storage projects from speculative toward a standard procurement decision for workspaces with facilities in high-solar-irradiance locations. The tariff risk on Chinese-manufactured components is a near-term procurement variable to manage, not a reason to defer.

**2. Fleet electrification roadmap sequencing.**

*Analytical inference:* the structural cost persistence in Europe and North America for new renewable build (Section 1) does not mean grid electricity is expensive in those markets; it means new build is slower. Road-fleet electrification decisions should be based on current commercial electricity tariff data in each operating region, not on new-build LCOE projections.

**3. Supplier sustainability claims scrutiny.**

*Operational implication:* the finding that most new utility-scale capacity is cheaper than new fossil-fuel capacity (Section 1) is a publicly available reference point. Workspaces receiving sustainability claims from energy suppliers, fleet operators, or logistics partners that position renewable energy as inherently more expensive can now challenge those claims with sourced data.

**4. What this finding does not resolve for decisions.**

*Analytical inference:* the report does not address transport-sector-specific energy costs (jet fuel, marine bunker fuel, diesel) directly; the connection between falling renewable LCOE and transport fuel costs runs through electrification, hydrogen, and e-fuels, each with its own cost and regulatory trajectory this source does not resolve. The forward cost trajectory is conditional on supply-chain stability that this source itself identifies as at risk; workspaces making multi-year capital commitments on solar or BESS should factor this uncertainty into project financing structures.

# 4. Client Conversation Talking Points and Public Position

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- Renewable electricity is now cheaper than fossil-fuel alternatives for the large majority of new utility-scale capacity globally; this is the 2024 cost reality documented by the source, not a projection.
- The cost of battery storage has fallen sharply since 2010, making on-site solar-plus-storage a standard infrastructure decision rather than a sustainability premium.

**Pitfalls to avoid:**

*Analytical inference:* do not claim global LCOE averages apply to specific facility costs; the sourced figures are global weighted averages, not site-level procurement prices, and a claim naming a specific per-kWh cost at a specific facility without a matching tariff quote is an overreach. Do not apply the global cost advantage to African-corridor operations without qualification; the source explicitly documents that the decline is not universal there. Do not claim the renewable cost advantage resolves SAF economics; SAF costs are governed by feedstock, conversion technology, blending mandates, and carbon-credit structures separate from renewable electricity LCOE.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific client sustainability disclosure can rely on this source's global weighted-average figures, versus requiring site-specific tariff evidence, is a matter for the client's own reporting counsel, not a determination this brief makes.

# 5. What the Finding Does Not Resolve

GAP: [does_not_resolve] Transport fuel costs (jet fuel, marine bunkers, diesel) are not present in the captured source blocks; this source covers power generation costs only, and the workspace's primary cost exposure on SAF surcharges and bunker-fuel adjustments is not addressed.

*Analytical inference:* the gap between the installed figure above and the COP28 tripling target implies an acceleration of annual additions well beyond the 2024 record cited in Section 1. Whether this acceleration materialises, and at what cost, is not established from the captured source blocks.

entries.body:
# 1. What the Research Found

**MONITORING. Re-check window: whether a peer-reviewed academic journal publication of the underlying methodology follows this public report, per the Nature Editorial's own stated publication plan.**

FACT: MIT's Climate Machine, with support from Coldplay, Warner Music Group, Live Nation, and Hope Solutions, released what the press release describes as "the first comprehensive annual carbon emissions calculation of the live music industry in the U.S. and U.K." on Dec 11, 2025. *Source: MIT Climate Machine / Warner Music Group press release, PR Newswire, Dec 11, 2025. https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/mit-climate-machine-with-support-from-coldplay-warner-music-group-live-nation-and-hope-solutions-release-first-ever-total-emissions-of-live-music-in-us-and-uk-302639267.html

FACT: the study "analyzes data from over 80,000 events across the U.S. and the U.K., capturing greenhouse gas emissions across all major impact areas including trucking, energy, food and beverage consumption, water, waste, fan travel, artist and crew travel, accommodation, and freight" *Source: PR Newswire, Dec 11, 2025. https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/mit-climate-machine-with-support-from-coldplay-warner-music-group-live-nation-and-hope-solutions-release-first-ever-total-emissions-of-live-music-in-us-and-uk-302639267.html

FACT: the report states the live music sector "accounts for just 0.2% of the U.S.'s and 1.1% of the U.K.'s total emissions" *Source: PR Newswire, Dec 11, 2025. https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/mit-climate-machine-with-support-from-coldplay-warner-music-group-live-nation-and-hope-solutions-release-first-ever-total-emissions-of-live-music-in-us-and-uk-302639267.html

FACT: "Grounded in rigorous peer-reviewed research, industry reports, and advanced analysis, the findings offer an unprecedented..." data-driven view of the sector, per the study's own description. *Source: PR Newswire, Dec 11, 2025. https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/mit-climate-machine-with-support-from-coldplay-warner-music-group-live-nation-and-hope-solutions-release-first-ever-total-emissions-of-live-music-in-us-and-uk-302639267.html

*Note:* the study's scope covers the US and UK only; generalisability to other markets is not addressed in the captured source material. The study covers a single annual calculation; longitudinal trend data is not described.

## Key quantitative findings

FACT: "Fan travel is the largest driver of live music emissions, accounting for 77% in the U.K. and 62% in the U.S. across nearly all event types." *Source: PR Newswire, Dec 11, 2025. https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/mit-climate-machine-with-support-from-coldplay-warner-music-group-live-nation-and-hope-solutions-release-first-ever-total-emissions-of-live-music-in-us-and-uk-302639267.html

FACT: "Food and beverage ranks next, contributing to 16.9% in the U.S. and 7.6% in the U.K., driven largely by animal-based products. A shift toward plant-based menus could reduce these emissions by 40% or more." *Source: PR Newswire, Dec 11, 2025. https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/mit-climate-machine-with-support-from-coldplay-warner-music-group-live-nation-and-hope-solutions-release-first-ever-total-emissions-of-live-music-in-us-and-uk-302639267.html

FACT: "emerge as major contributors–trucking makes up 14% of U.S. emissions, while air freight accounts for nearly 35% in the U.K." *Source: PR Newswire, Dec 11, 2025. https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/mit-climate-machine-with-support-from-coldplay-warner-music-group-live-nation-and-hope-solutions-release-first-ever-total-emissions-of-live-music-in-us-and-uk-302639267.html

FACT: "Large-format shows, though fewer in number, generate a disproportionate share of total emissions, making festivals and stadium tours powerful catalysts for innovation and scalable climate solutions." *Source: PR Newswire, Dec 11, 2025. https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/mit-climate-machine-with-support-from-coldplay-warner-music-group-live-nation-and-hope-solutions-release-first-ever-total-emissions-of-live-music-in-us-and-uk-302639267.html

## Adjacent corroborating work

FACT: "The resulting roadmap, published in 2021 (see go.nature.com/3xdyq5j ), set out emissions-reduction targets for the UK live music industry in line with the 2015 Paris climate agreement.", per research produced at a UK university climate research centre. *Source: Nature Editorial, 04 September 2024 (corrected 18 September 2024). https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-024-02828-1

FACT: a battery-powered live outdoor concert headlined by a UK band, attended by more than 32,000 fans, "slashed energy-related greenhouse-gas emissions by 98%, according to a report by climate researchers" *Source: Nature Career News, 25 March 2025. https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-025-00753-5

FACT: a 2010 study "used figures from 2007 to estimate that the UK music industry produced some 540,000 tonnes of greenhouse-gas emissions annually, around 0.1% of the country’s total energy-related carbon dioxide emissions. Live music accounted for 74% of that." *Source: Nature Editorial, 04 September 2024. https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-024-02828-1

*Analytical inference:* the jump from roughly 0.1% of UK energy-related CO2 in the 2010 study to 1.1% of UK total emissions in the 2025 MIT study likely reflects differences in scope (total GHG versus energy CO2 only) and methodology, and the industry's growth since then, rather than a simple like-for-like increase; no direct methodological comparison is available in the captured source material to confirm this.

# 2. Why This Finding Matters Operationally and Commercially

The freight and logistics implications of this study are specific and direct. When fan travel is excluded, air freight is the single largest emissions contributor in the UK live music supply chain at nearly 35% of remaining emissions, and trucking is the second-largest contributor in the US at 14% (Section 1). This is the finding most directly actionable for operators providing freight, logistics, and transportation services to live events clients.

*Operational implication:* for workspaces providing air freight, road freight, or multimodal logistics services to the live events sector, covering equipment, staging, production materials, artist merchandise, and time-sensitive cargo, this study creates a direct, documented emissions profile for the category. Clients including promoters, tour operators, venue managers, and artist management teams now have quantified data showing freight's share of their total environmental impact.

*Analytical inference:* the disproportionate emissions share attributed to air freight in the UK context is consistent with the well-documented carbon intensity of air versus road or ocean freight per tonne-km. For workspaces whose live-events clients are concentrated in UK touring, where air freight of production equipment between tour legs is common, this finding signals that client-facing emissions reporting on freight will become an expected deliverable, not a differentiator.

*Analytical inference:* the report's identification of large-format shows as generating a disproportionate share of total emissions (Section 1) points specifically to the stadium tour and major festival segment, the highest-volume, highest-value freight accounts for logistics providers. This is the segment where sustainability scrutiny will concentrate first.

*Operational implication:* a company representative of one of the study's funders was quoted describing the data as enabling more coordinated action in partnership with artists, venues and fans, signalling that procurement conversations within that company's own supply chain are likely to reference this study. *Source: Music Week. https://www.musicweek.com/live/read/backed-by-coldplay-warner-music-and-live-nation-mit-s-climate-machine-reports-on-us-uk-emissions/093247

# 3. What the Finding Changes for Strategy, Claims, or Decisions

**1. Emissions reporting and client data requests.**

*Operational implication:* the study establishes a new industry baseline. Workspaces that currently lack the ability to report emissions on live-events freight accounts, at the shipment, tour leg, or annual contract level, are now behind a documented standard. The study does not itself impose any reporting obligation, but it creates an evidentiary foundation client-driven sustainability requirements can reference.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific client contract already contains sustainability reporting obligations that this study's publication triggers, either through reference to industry baselines or through general ESG clauses, depends on the specific contract language and jurisdiction; counsel review of existing live-events client agreements is warranted.

**2. Modal shift decisions.**

*Analytical inference:* the air freight share in UK live music emissions is driven by the carbon intensity of air freight per unit weight-distance. Where tour schedules allow road alternatives, particularly for UK and European routing where overnight road freight is technically substitutable for short-haul air, the study gives clients a quantified reason to request modal alternatives. Workspaces offering multimodal solutions are better positioned than single-mode air specialists to respond to this demand.

**3. Sustainability credentials and SAF.**

*Analytical inference:* the study's air freight finding in the UK makes sustainable aviation fuel a directly relevant lever for workspaces holding air freight accounts on UK and international touring routes. SAF availability and cost remain constrained; the workspace's ability to offer SAF-blended air freight as a premium product tier to live-events clients is a near-term commercial differentiator, provided the workspace can secure access through carrier programmes. No SAF supplier relationships are assumed here; this requires workspace-specific procurement verification.

# 4. Client Conversation Talking Points and Public Position

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- The MIT Climate Machine study, published Dec 11, 2025, is the first comprehensive, peer-reviewed-grounded annual carbon calculation for the live music industry in the US and UK, covering more than 80,000 events across all major emissions categories. It is a citable, authoritative reference.
- The study identifies freight and trucking as the largest emissions contributors in the live music supply chain after fan travel is set aside, air freight at nearly 35% of remaining UK emissions, trucking at 14% in the US. This gives the workspace a factual basis for positioning freight emissions reduction as directly relevant to client sustainability targets.

**Pitfalls to avoid:**

*Analytical inference:* do not cite this study as establishing a compliance obligation on freight providers; it does not. It is a research and industry-baseline document, not a regulation. Do not claim that the workspace's freight services are already aligned with the study's findings without verifiable emissions data to support the claim. Do not present the 40% food-and-beverage reduction estimate as applicable to freight; it is specific to the food and beverage category only. Do not assert that the UK air freight figure applies directly to any specific client account; the figure is an industry aggregate, and account-level data requires measurement.

# 5. What the Finding Does Not Resolve

GAP: [does_not_resolve] Whether equivalent emissions profiles apply to European, Asia-Pacific, Latin American, or other touring markets is not present in the captured source blocks; the study covers the US and UK only, and its freight findings cannot be extrapolated to other markets without further research.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] A standardised per-event, per-shipment, or per-tonne-km calculation methodology that freight providers can directly adopt is not present in the captured source blocks; the study establishes industry-aggregate and category-share figures, not an accounting standard.

GAP: [methodology_limits] Whether a separate peer-reviewed academic journal publication of the underlying methodology has been completed and published, beyond this public report, is not confirmed in the captured source blocks; the Nature Editorial's own stated publication plan referenced a later academic report.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] The study does not itself create a regulatory obligation, reporting requirement, or emissions limit; any future citation of it in a regulatory consultation or licensing framework is not present in the captured source blocks.

**Monitoring calendar (this research_finding's own timeline section, per its format's section list):**

- Dec 11, 2025: the MIT Climate Machine / Warner Music Group press release, this brief's primary source, was published.

# 1. What the Research Found

**MONITORING. Re-check window: Q4 2026 for interim JOLT publications; Q1-Q2 2027 for the programme's primary reporting window.**

**Programme identity and current phase.** Project JOLT (Joint Operators Logistics Trial) is an active, real-world trial programme focused on electric heavy goods vehicles at 44-tonne operational weight. It was Project Jolt (Joint Operators Logistics Trial) was officially launched at an event hosted by Nestle in York on 26th March, 2025.. As of February 2026 the project is in its third "round-robin" round, meaning operators rotate vehicles across progressively more demanding logistics lanes. *Source: Centre for Sustainable Road Freight (CSRF), "Latest news from Project JOLT," 11th February 2026. https://www.csrf.ac.uk/2026/02/latest-news-from-project-jolt-2/

FACT: "Project JOLT brings together a consortium of leading industry partners, including John Lewis Partnership. Volvo Trucks UK, and Flexible Power Systems" *Source: CSRF, "Latest news from Project JOLT," 11th February 2026. https://www.csrf.ac.uk/2026/02/latest-news-from-project-jolt-2/

FACT: "This has resulted in 9 eHGVs and a number of diesel comparator vehicles having installed data loggers and generating high-resolution performance data." *Source: CSRF, "Latest news from Project JOLT." https://www.csrf.ac.uk/2026/02/latest-news-from-project-jolt-2/

FACT: "Charging facilities are provided by Evyve or in some cases by the hauliers themselves. In addition, some hauliers are using their own eHGVs." *Source: CSRF, "Latest news from Project JOLT." https://www.csrf.ac.uk/2026/02/latest-news-from-project-jolt-2/

FACT: "There are four main dimensions – logistics, energy supply, infrastructure and finance." *Source: CSRF, "Latest news from Project JOLT." https://www.csrf.ac.uk/2026/02/latest-news-from-project-jolt-2/

FACT: "Data is also being collected from the OEM telematics systems, from the Chargers and from Logistics systems." *Source: CSRF, "Latest news from Project JOLT." https://www.csrf.ac.uk/2026/02/latest-news-from-project-jolt-2/

*Analytical inference:* the research team's own account states it is "Prof David Cebon and his team are analysing the wealth of data, reporting back to the project participants and bringing greater certainty to these issues.", which places JOLT's current output as interim practitioner data shared with participants, not a published peer-reviewed conclusion. *Source: CSRF, "Latest news from Project JOLT." https://www.csrf.ac.uk/2026/02/latest-news-from-project-jolt-2/

FACT: "Fleet Operators tend to start with relatively simple shuttle operations, before feeling more confident to test their longer lanes." *Source: CSRF, "Latest news from Project JOLT." https://www.csrf.ac.uk/2026/02/latest-news-from-project-jolt-2/

FACT: "Initial haulier concerns remain capital cost, payload and range." *Source: CSRF, "Project Jolt Launch, Media Reports," 18th April 2025. https://www.csrf.ac.uk/2025/04/project-jolt-launch-media-reports/

FACT: "For the next two years the project will gather, analyse and report extensive data to evidence the commercial and operational impact of electrification on fleets." *Source: CSRF, "Project Jolt Launch, Media Reports." https://www.csrf.ac.uk/2025/04/project-jolt-launch-media-reports/

*Note:* JOLT is an industry-academic consortium trial generating real-world operational data, not a modelled or laboratory study; it does not yet publish peer-reviewed output.

**Independent academic corroboration of long-haul decarbonisation challenges.**

FACT: "the inclusion of intangible costs triggers a shift, leading to the emergence of hydrogen fuel cell vehicles for heavy trucks, while battery electric vehicles are preferred for medium and small trucks." *Source: a 2024 peer-reviewed study in Nature Scientific Reports modelling decarbonisation pathways for heavy, medium, and light trucks. https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-52682-4

FACT: "implicit costs related to range anxiety and charging inconvenience constitute at least 27% of the perceived cost of ZEVs, making them uncompetitive." *Source: same Nature Scientific Reports study, 24 January 2024. https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-52682-4

**UK regulatory and investment context.**

FACT: "The Zero Emission HGV and Infrastructure Demonstrator (ZEHID) programme, backed by circa £200m in funding from the Department for Transport and delivered in partnership with Innovate UK, is rising to meet this challenge. With a bold vision to deploy around 350 of the heaviest battery-electric and hydrogen fuel cell vehicles on UK roads, the programme will also fund and support over 70 public and depot-based infrastructure installations by 2030." *Source: Innovate UK Business Connect, "Zero emission heavy goods vehicles and infrastructure" (ZEHID). https://iuk-business-connect.org.uk/programme/zero-emission-heavy-goods-vehicles-and-infrastructure/

FACT: "Procurement and Infrastructure Development (2024–2026): Building the foundation with critical charging and refuelling infrastructure." *Source: Innovate UK Business Connect, ZEHID. https://iuk-business-connect.org.uk/programme/zero-emission-heavy-goods-vehicles-and-infrastructure/

FACT: "On-Road Demonstration (2026–2031): Real-world trials of zero-emission HGVs, testing their capabilities in various duty cycles and operational scenarios." *Source: Innovate UK Business Connect, ZEHID. https://iuk-business-connect.org.uk/programme/zero-emission-heavy-goods-vehicles-and-infrastructure/

FACT: "Data collection is critical to this programme and so Ricardo have been engaged to independently evaluate all projects. The learning will be both public and fed to the Department for Transport." *Source: Innovate UK Business Connect, ZEHID. https://iuk-business-connect.org.uk/programme/zero-emission-heavy-goods-vehicles-and-infrastructure/

*Analytical inference:* JOLT sits within, and generates data relevant to, the broader ZEHID and policy ecosystem; JOLT's practitioner-facing findings are likely to inform ZEHID's on-road demonstration phase and UK policy calibration on whether purchase-price or operational-expenditure incentives dominate UK HGV decarbonisation support. The two programmes are structurally complementary: ZEHID provides infrastructure and deployment capital, JOLT provides operational and financial data on real logistics operations at scale.

# 2. Why This Finding Matters Operationally and Commercially

**Mechanism for road-freight operations.** The core mechanism is a tripartite barrier, capital cost, payload penalty, and range constraint, operating simultaneously on the same vehicle. For freight operations relying on long-haul road legs, none of these three barriers resolves independently of the others; a vehicle with adequate range may carry a reduced payload, and a vehicle with adequate payload may be range-constrained on high-density lanes. The JOLT data is capturing where these trade-offs land in real UK logistics operations, not in simulation.

*Operational implication:* for workspaces where road transport supports time-critical or high-density lanes, including road legs feeding air freight gateways, repositioning of empty freight equipment, or final-leg delivery for event logistics, film, or fine-art cargo, the payload and range constraints identified by JOLT participants directly affect whether an electric HGV can replace a diesel tractor unit on a given lane without operational redesign.

FACT: "A major concern that is starting to surface is how to provide electricity supply connections for high-power charging infrastructure." *Source: CSRF, "Project Jolt Launch, Media Reports," 18th April 2025. https://www.csrf.ac.uk/2025/04/project-jolt-launch-media-reports/

*Analytical inference:* grid connection timelines for high-power depot charging in the UK are widely reported to run from roughly a year to several years depending on local distribution network operator capacity; this is an untracked variable in most operator total-cost-of-ownership models and represents a lead-time risk that precedes any vehicle procurement decision. The ZEHID programme explicitly funds infrastructure deployment to address this, but its on-road demonstration timeline (Section 1) implies the supply constraint will remain acute through mid-decade.

*Analytical inference:* the Nature Scientific Reports modelling finding (Section 1) that including intangible costs specifically triggers a technology shift for heavy trucks, not medium or light, toward hydrogen, while battery-electric vehicles remain dominant for lighter categories, is directly relevant to 44-tonne long-haul operations of the kind JOLT is trialling: the technology economics for this weight and range band are less settled than for urban or regional delivery.

FACT: "Postponing action to achieve decarbonisation pathway will result in a quicker utilisation of the carbon budget by easier-to-abate sectors. This will leave hard-to-abate sectors, including road freight, with less time to implement necessary infrastructure and investments for decarbonisation" *Source: Nature Scientific Reports, 2024. https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-52682-4

FACT: "ain, but they also account for a significant 20% of domestic transport CO2 emissions. As the nation races toward it" *Source: Innovate UK Business Connect, ZEHID programme page. https://iuk-business-connect.org.uk/programme/zero-emission-heavy-goods-vehicles-and-infrastructure/

# 3. What the Finding Changes for Strategy, Claims, or Decisions

**1. Road carrier selection and subcontractor qualification.**

*Analytical inference:* freight forwarders placing road trunking and line-haul subcontracts should now treat electric-HGV capability, charging infrastructure status, and data-logging participation as carrier qualification variables, not because compliance requires it yet, but because carriers in JOLT or ZEHID trials are generating auditable operational data that will become the baseline for Scope 3 carrier-specific emission factors as disclosure requirements tighten.

*Analytical inference:* under ISO 14083, the international standard for quantifying GHG emissions from transport chain operations, freight forwarders calculating Scope 3 Category 4 emissions must either use carrier-specific data or default to published emission factors that will increasingly diverge from electric-HGV-equipped carrier actuals. Early alignment with JOLT-participating carriers creates a Scope 3 data advantage before the data is required.

**2. Client sustainability commitments, avoid premature precision.**

*Analytical inference:* the JOLT trial is in Phase 3 of a two-year programme; final quantitative outputs (total cost of ownership, battery degradation curves, logistics cost differentials, charging strategies) have not yet been published. Any claims made in client conversations about road freight electrification readiness that cite JOLT should be scoped to Phase 3 status and operational observations, not to conclusions the programme has not yet reached.

**3. Infrastructure lead-time as a procurement planning variable.**

*Analytical inference:* for workspaces that own or operate depot facilities, or that have clients whose distribution networks include depot charging questions, the finding that electricity supply connections are a surfacing concern (Section 2) means infrastructure lead-time should enter planning conversations now. Operators not engaged in either JOLT or ZEHID are not currently building the infrastructure data or grid connection queue position that will be needed for electric-HGV adoption at scale from 2027 onward.

**4. Policy targeting signals a shift in commercial incentive structure.**

*Analytical inference:* the Nature Scientific Reports finding that policy should target operational expenditure rather than purchase-price incentives (Section 1) is a directional signal for how UK and EU support mechanisms may evolve. For freight principals negotiating multi-year road carrier contracts with sustainability clauses, the relevant question shifts from vehicle price toward per-km or per-tonne operational cost under an operating-expenditure-targeting incentive regime, favouring mileage-based green premiums over one-off capital contribution clauses.

# 4. Client Conversation Talking Points and Public Position

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- The UK's most structured real-world trial of 44-tonne electric HGVs is currently in its third round of operator testing, with nine vehicles and diesel comparators generating high-resolution performance data, involving more than 20 industry partners.
- The headline barriers being measured in the trial, capital cost, payload, and range, are confirmed in independent peer-reviewed research as the factors most likely to drive heavy-truck operators toward hydrogen over battery-electric if not addressed through operational-expenditure policy support.
- The electricity supply connection for high-power depot charging is identified as an emergent constraint beyond the vehicles themselves, meaning the infrastructure timeline is as important as technology readiness in planning any road fleet transition.

**Pitfalls to avoid:**

*Analytical inference:* do not claim that JOLT has published total-cost-of-ownership conclusions or that the business case for 44-tonne electric HGVs is resolved; the trial explicitly states it is still gathering and reporting data. Do not assert that battery-electric is definitively the preferred technology for long-haul heavy freight; the academic modelling shows intangible costs shift the optimal technology toward hydrogen for heavy trucks, and JOLT has not yet published conclusions on this. Do not cite JOLT Phase 3 data as peer-reviewed or audited output; it is practitioner-facing interim data shared with participants.

**Questions to pose to road carrier partners and logistics clients:**

- Is your primary road carrier participating in JOLT, ZEHID, or any comparable electric-HGV trial, and what data are they generating on the lanes relevant to this freight?
- What is your depot's current grid connection capacity for high-power charging, and what is the lead time for upgrade with your distribution network operator?

# 5. What the Finding Does Not Resolve

GAP: [does_not_resolve] The technology winner for long-haul heavy freight is not yet resolved; JOLT Phase 3 is generating data, not publishing conclusions, and the academic modelling was conducted for Ireland's energy system, which may not transfer directly to UK cost and grid structures. *Legal Confirmation Required:* no regulatory determination has been published designating battery-electric as the mandated technology pathway for UK HGVs above a defined gross vehicle weight.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] Grid connection lead times are not quantified in the captured source blocks; the CSRF launch reporting surfaces electricity supply connections as a concern but does not provide data on connection timelines or costs for specific depot types or distribution network operator regions.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] JOLT's final findings are pending; following the launch in March 2025, the two-year programme's primary reporting is expected approximately Q1-Q2 2027. Until that window, total-cost-of-ownership curves, battery degradation profiles, charging strategy conclusions, and logistics cost differentials remain unquantified from this programme.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] Hydrogen pathway readiness is not addressed by JOLT; JOLT is a battery-electric trial, and the parallel hydrogen pathway trialled under ZEHID's own hydrogen-focused projects is a separate programme with separate participants and timeline.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] No cost figures for JOLT vehicles, charging, or logistics operations are available in the captured source blocks; capital cost, per-km operational cost, and charging infrastructure cost data are being reported back to participants but have not been publicly released as of the date of this pass.

GAP: [methodology_limits] A CSRF-linked trade-press source naming specific operators and vehicle-operator pairings could not be accessed in this capture pool; detail from that source has not been used in this brief and is flagged as a retrieval gap.

- 2030: the ZEHID deployment target date falls due.

entries.body:
# 1. What the Research Found

**MONITORING. Re-check window: WEO-2026, expected in 2026 based on the IEA's annual publication cadence since 1998; the next scheduled edition that would update scenario data and address the APS gap.**

**Scope and release.** The IEA published the World Energy Outlook 2025 as a flagship report on "12 November 2025". A free dataset accompanies the report. *Source: Global Energy and Climate Model, IEA. https://www.iea.org/reports/global-energy-and-climate-model

FACT: "WEO-2025 Free Dataset includes world aggregated data for all three modelled scenarios (CPS, STEPS, NZE) and selected data for key regions and countries for 2035, 2040 and 2050, as well as historical data (2010, 2023, 2024)." *Source: World Energy Outlook 2025 Extended Dataset, IEA. https://www.iea.org/data-and-statistics/data-product/world-energy-outlook-2025-extended-dataset

**Scenario architecture, a structural change for 2025.**

FACT: "The World Energy Outlook 2025 ( WEO-2025 ) has three main scenarios. Two of these set starting conditions and then examine where they lead – the Current Policies Scenario (CPS) and the Stated Policies Scenario (STEPS). A third, the Net Zero Emissions by 2050 (NZE) Scenario, maps out a pathway to achieve specific energy and climate-related goals." *Source: World Energy Outlook 2025 Executive Summary, IEA. https://www.iea.org/reports/world-energy-outlook-2025/executive-summary

FACT: "The WEO this year will not include the Announced Pledges Scenario (APS)." The IEA commentary explains this is because "many countries are yet to announce or update their targets, and an update to the APS would give only a partial picture of the implications for energy and emissions." *Source: Scenarios in the World Energy Outlook 2025, IEA, 05 November 2025. https://www.iea.org/commentaries/scenarios-in-the-world-energy-outlook-2025

FACT: "None of the scenarios in the WEO are a forecast." *Source: Scenarios in the World Energy Outlook 2025, IEA. https://www.iea.org/commentaries/scenarios-in-the-world-energy-outlook-2025

**Scope limitation, what the free dataset does not contain.**

FACT: the WEO-2025 Extended Dataset is a separate paid product, listed at "€ 685" for a single-user digital licence. "WEO-2025 Extended Dataset includes more detailed information at regional and country-level for CPS and STEPS (including detailed energy balance, electrical capacity, electricity generation, CO2 emission by region, economic and activity indicators, etc.) across projected years (2035, 2040, 2045, 2050) as well as historical data (2010, 2015, 2023, 2024)." *Source: World Energy Outlook 2025 Extended Dataset, IEA. https://www.iea.org/data-and-statistics/data-product/world-energy-outlook-2025-extended-dataset

FACT: "The Extended Dataset also includes WEO-2025 chapter figures, investment, trade and power sector capacity addition and retirement, fossil fuel prices, refining capacity and runs, power generation technology costs and assumptions and air pollution data." *Source: World Energy Outlook 2025 Extended Dataset, IEA. https://www.iea.org/data-and-statistics/data-product/world-energy-outlook-2025-extended-dataset

*Analytical inference:* workspaces that download the free dataset gain world-aggregate scenario trajectories sufficient for directional planning and scenario comparison, but lack the country- and regional-level energy balance, investment, and fossil-fuel-price data needed to model corridor-specific cost impacts or carrier procurement assumptions with precision; those decisions require the paid Extended Dataset or a separate modelling licence.

# 2. Why This Finding Matters Operationally and Commercially

FACT: "road freight is responsible for around 40% of road transport energy demand today, more than 90% of which is fuelled by oil." *Source: China steers global shift to electric freight, IEA reports, Motor Transport, 13 November 2025. https://motortransport.co.uk/china-steers-global-shift-to-electric-freight-iea-reports/52669.article

*Operational implication:* for workspaces with road freight as a secondary transport mode, including drayage from air gateways and last-mile delivery of high-value and time-sensitive cargo, a Current Policies Scenario trajectory of rising heavy-truck energy demand through 2035, predominantly oil-fuelled, translates to sustained exposure to diesel price volatility and emerging CO2-standard compliance costs on European and other regulated corridors.

**HGV electrification, pace diverges sharply by scenario.**

FACT: "accounted for just under 3% of global heavy freight trucks sold in 2024 and this rises to around 15% of global sales in 2035, mainly in China and the European Union" "Electrification is also reaching vehicle types that traditionally have been challenging to progress beyond oil use. In the STEPS by 2050, nearly 25 per cent of the global heavy truck fleet is electrified, a total of around 25 million vehicles" *Source: Motor Transport, 13 November 2025. https://motortransport.co.uk/china-steers-global-shift-to-electric-freight-iea-reports/52669.article

*Operational implication:* the 10-percentage-point gap between the two scenarios in HGV electrification represents meaningful uncertainty for workspaces assessing when to require electric-vehicle capability from road carriers on EU or UK corridors; the more conservative trajectory implies a longer window of diesel dependence for carriers.

**Critical minerals supply chain risk.**

FACT: "A single country is the dominant refiner for 19 out of 20 energy-related strategic minerals, with an average market share of around 70%." *Source: World Energy Outlook 2025 Executive Summary, IEA. https://www.iea.org/reports/world-energy-outlook-2025/executive-summary

*Analytical inference:* this concentration finding is directly relevant to workspaces moving electrification-related cargo, EV components, batteries, charging infrastructure, on air and ocean lanes, particularly on Asia-origin corridors.

**Hydrogen and LNG in freight.**

FACT: in the Current Policies Scenario, "powertrains such as hydrogen take only 1% of global sales." *Source: Motor Transport, 13 November 2025. https://motortransport.co.uk/china-steers-global-shift-to-electric-freight-iea-reports/52669.article

*Analytical inference:* LNG's projected growth in long-haul trucking represents a fuel transition pathway that reduces but does not eliminate oil dependency, while introducing LNG price exposure; for workspaces relying on long-haul road carriers in China or cross-border Asia lanes, carrier fleet composition is shifting in ways that require updated emissions accounting assumptions.

# 3. What the Finding Changes for Strategy, Claims, or Decisions

**1. Scenario selection for planning.**

*Analytical inference:* the reintroduction of the Current Policies Scenario as the most conservative, enacted-policy-only scenario, and the removal of the Announced Pledges Scenario, changes how workspaces should use this data for internal planning and client-facing sustainability commitments. Workspaces that previously cited the retired scenario's trajectories in sustainability reports or carrier RFPs need to revisit the scenario reference they use.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether substituting a different scenario for the retired one in published sustainability reports or scope 3 baseline calculations satisfies the methodology requirements of a specific disclosure framework requires compliance counsel and framework guidance review.

**2. Road carrier procurement clauses.**

*Analytical inference:* the divergence between the conservative and policy-trajectory scenarios in HGV electrification share means that contractual commitments requiring carriers to operate a specific proportion of electric vehicles by a given date are scenario-sensitive. Workspaces inserting or renegotiating EV-fleet clauses in road carrier contracts should specify which scenario trajectory the requirement is calibrated against, or use a review-trigger mechanism tied to published IEA updates.

**3. Scope 3 emissions modelling.**

*Analytical inference:* workspaces using the free dataset for Scope 3 carrier emissions modelling gain world-aggregate fuel-mix trajectory data sufficient for directional scenario analysis; country- and corridor-level granularity needed to model specific lane emissions accurately requires the paid Extended Dataset or a separate modelling licence. Workspaces that represent specific corridor-level emission projections to clients without this data face a methodology gap.

**4. Connection to EU CO2 standards for heavy trucks.**

*Analytical inference:* the finding that EU CO2 standards are a primary driver of HGV electrification in Europe, alongside cost competitiveness in China, links directly to the EU Heavy Duty Vehicle CO2 regulation. Workspaces monitoring whether road carriers will have electrified fleets available on EU corridors within contract horizons should track EU CO2 standard review cycles, not only WEO updates. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the specific fleet-share obligations and timelines under the EU Heavy Duty Vehicle CO2 regulation, as they bind carriers on the workspace's EU road lanes, require legal and carrier-specific confirmation.

# 4. Client Conversation Talking Points and Public Position

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- The IEA's 2025 World Energy Outlook, its most authoritative annual dataset, projects heavy truck electrification reaching around 15% of global sales by 2035 under its conservative scenario, with the EU and China as the primary adoption markets. This is a sourced, citable finding from the flagship report.
- Under no WEO-2025 scenario does oil cease to dominate transport energy use through 2035. This is factually accurate and positions the workspace honestly against premature decarbonisation claims.
- The IEA's free dataset covers world-aggregate trajectories to 2050 across all three modelled scenarios; it is publicly available and can be cited in sustainability discussions without a licence.

**Pitfalls to avoid:**

*Analytical inference:* do not cite retired-scenario trajectories as current IEA guidance; that scenario has been formally removed from WEO-2025 and will not be restored until a more complete national-pledge picture is available. Do not claim the remaining scenarios represent IEA predictions or forecasts; the IEA is explicit that none of its scenarios are a forecast. Do not present the free dataset's aggregate figures as country- or corridor-level data; country-level detail sits in the paid Extended Dataset only. Do not cite specific fossil fuel price projections, investment figures, or air pollution data from the free dataset; those variables are in the paid Extended Dataset only.

**Question to pose to clients:** is your current emissions baseline or supplier sustainability scorecard anchored to any specific IEA scenario, and if it was using the now-retired scenario, has that been updated?

# 5. What the Finding Does Not Resolve

GAP: [does_not_resolve] Corridor- and lane-level cost impact is not present in the captured source blocks; the free dataset provides world-aggregate and selected-region data only, and corridor-specific fuel cost modelling depends on the paid Extended Dataset or a separate model licence.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] Aircraft fuel trajectory and SAF deployment rates under any scenario are not present in the captured source blocks; this is a material gap for workspaces where air is the primary transport mode.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] Corridor-specific ocean shipping fuel mix projections, and the gap between the sourced shipping trajectory and FuelEU Maritime or EU ETS compliance requirements, are not present in the captured source blocks.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] No date or process for reinstating the retired scenario has been announced in the captured source blocks; the IEA has stated it will be revisited once a more complete picture of national pledges is available.

GAP: [does_not_resolve] The policy-trajectory scenario's hydrogen outlook for heavy trucks beyond 2035 is not present in the captured source blocks.

GAP: [methodology_limits] Freight-specific numeric detail in this brief is drawn from a single trade-press analysis of the WEO-2025 dataset, not from the IEA's own primary report text on freight, which was not captured at that level of detail in this pass's source blocks.

**Monitoring calendar (this research_finding's own timeline section, per its format's section list):**
- 12 November 2025: the World Energy Outlook 2025 flagship report was published.
- 05 November 2025: the IEA's own scenario-architecture commentary, explaining the scenario changes for 2025, was published.
- 2035: the scenario checkpoints for HGV electrification share and critical-minerals concentration (Section 2) fall due; the next scheduled checkpoint for this forecast.
